narrative.overview: The visual language of the Employee HRIS & Leave Management System is calibrated for high-consequence administrative reliability and employee self-service efficiency. Operating primarily in Operate mode, the system treats screen real estate as a precision tool: typography is legible and compact, spatial margins are rhythmic and predictable, and cognitive friction is minimized through strict visual hierarchy.
keyCharacteristics: Restrained Density: Information-rich layouts that stay uncluttered through consistent 4px-based spatial multiples.
Calm, High-Contrast Palette: Slate neutrals paired with a decisive Cobalt Blue accent and WCAG AA-compliant semantic alerts.
Tactile State Elevation: Flat-at-rest surfaces that lift delicately on hover and state transitions to provide tactile confidence.
Dual-Channel Status Clarity: Every critical status indicator combines color, text, and shape to guarantee accessibility.

rules.name: The 10% Intentionality Rule
rules.body: Cobalt Blue is reserved exclusively for the single primary page action, active navigation link, or focus ring. It must never exceed 10% of any screen's surface area. Its rarity is the visual signal of importance.

rules.name: The Dual-Channel Status Rule
rules.body: No status may ever be communicated by color alone. Every badge, chip, and banner must combine a semantic background, accessible foreground text, and an explicit icon or geometric dot.

rules.name: The System Native Rule
rules.body: Do not load external web fonts for authenticated application screens. System fonts guarantee sub-millisecond initial paint times, zero layout shifts, and offline resilience.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: All cards, tables, and buttons rest flat with a 1px border. Shadows are never decorative; they appear only in response to user state.

dos: Do preserve the strict 2-Role boundary between HR administrative oversight and Employee self-service views.
Do ensure every interactive element has an accessible :focus-visible ring (2px solid #1D4ED8, offset 2px).
Do pair every semantic color status badge with an explicit 6px shape dot and readable text.
Do keep cards and table surfaces clean and flat-at-rest, using shadows only for interactive elevation.
Do maintain a minimum 4.5:1 text-to-background contrast ratio on all informational text.
donts: Don't introduce flashy neon gradients, floating glassmorphic blobs, or playful consumer SaaS micro-copy.
Don't use Cobalt Blue for generic non-actionable decoration or non-clickable text.
Don't allow leave approval or rejection actions without an immediate disabled state and loading confirmation.
Don't hide table columns on mobile without providing a clean, accessible stacked-card fallback.
Don't load heavy external client-side CSS or font frameworks; rely on native system fonts and local CSS tokens.
